# Full parity census, November 27, 2026

Status: DONE for the census and queue. Full product parity is not claimed. No product code was changed. Historical provider-only exclusions are reopened for review, not silently promoted to implementation gaps.

All 818 existing Markdown reports under this directory were searched in bounded local text reads for full SHAs, 12-character SHA references, source-qualified PR links and scope exclusions. Inventory-only files are not treated as dispositions. 188 unique OmniRoute commit rows and 2001 unique source-qualified open-PR rows are listed below. The 9router compare is identical, with zero delta commits. OmniRoute compare reports ahead_by=188, behind_by=0, total_commits=188 and merge base equal to the issue-comment baseline. The independently paginated newer-base comparison has exactly 158 commits, all contained in the 188-row collection.

116 commit rows and 117 open heads have no matching full or 12-character SHA in a non-inventory report. This means review is required; it does not establish a missing feature. Rows with evidence retain links to their prior assessment. A matching SHA alone does not validate that assessment, especially when its original scope was narrower. Commit-to-PR associations were also fetched for all 188 commits through GitHub GraphQL associatedPullRequests, in bounded batches of 30 commits with 20 PRs per commit; every hasNextPage was false. The associated-PR column and PR-level follow-ups link prior implementation evidence even when the branch commit SHA or current PR head was never recorded. These are reconciliation leads, not proof of parity at a changed head.

## Reproduce the collection

Use `gh api --paginate` on each endpoint. Fetch branch heads first and use their full SHAs for comparisons; a moving branch name is not a stable end boundary. With this installed gh version, `--slurp` is unavailable; `--jq ".[]"` or `--jq ".commits[]"` emits one JSON object per line across pages.

```sh
gh api repos/decolua/9router/commits/master
gh api repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/commits/release/v3.8.55
gh api --paginate 'repos/decolua/9router/pulls?state=open&per_page=100' --jq '.[]'
gh api --paginate 'repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/pulls?state=open&per_page=100' --jq '.[]'
gh api --paginate 'repos/decolua/9router/compare/5ae63d22847e07042e235b40e1d926b65e509013...5ae63d22847e07042e235b40e1d926b65e509013?per_page=100'
gh api --paginate 'repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/compare/6d99c052a58d8de0771b211c1181bbc1e3e354ef...c71f0065a7efe9230ec23b96a12253b050c4d7ad?per_page=100' --jq '.commits[]'
gh api --paginate 'repos/diegosouzapw/OmniRoute/compare/4de5c9b65f4cd1f966dbdf09c9d6ff510baa97a1...c71f0065a7efe9230ec23b96a12253b050c4d7ad?per_page=100' --jq '.commits[]'
gh api --paginate 'repos/bloodf/durindoor/pulls?state=open&per_page=100'
```

The compare API includes commits reachable through merged branches, not just first-parent merge commits. Keep these rows but implement each behavior once. A merge commit and its branch commits are not independent port requests. Future refreshes should diff by source plus full SHA; reopened scope reviews should also consult final per-port reports by PR identity.

## Targeted reconciliation units before any port

1. `parity-spend-observability-review`: reopen [9router #5906](https://github.com/decolua/9router/pull/5906) at `409f7623346382a3d544d0f32bf559d409e7a3fe`, previously excluded in [1072-nov27-e.md](1072-nov27-e.md). The local `src/lib/apiKeyLimits.js` already enforces dailyBudget/weeklyBudget/monthlyBudget and `src/sse/services/apiKeyPolicy.js` enforces lifetime costs. Do not port a second budget engine. Compare only uncovered metrics, price-source presentation and budget eligibility semantics. Files at risk: those two files, `src/lib/db/repos/apiKeysRepo.js`, `open-sse/providers/pricing.js`, `open-sse/handlers/chatCore/requestDetail.js`, `open-sse/handlers/chatCore.js`. Upstream metrics modules being absent is not enough to declare the full PR missing.
2. `parity-stream-usage-review`: reconcile [9router #5904](https://github.com/decolua/9router/pull/5904) against the already ported #5890 in [1072-nov27-b.md](1072-nov27-b.md). Check trailing-usage timing and fallback fixtures first. Files at risk: `open-sse/translator/response/openai-to-claude.js`, `open-sse/utils/stream.js`, `open-sse/utils/usageTracking.js`. The #5904 scope exclusion does not establish a remaining gap.
3. `parity-claude-observed-quota-review`: compare [OmniRoute #21406](https://github.com/cheaper-inference/OmniRoute/pull/21406) at `6dae88bfe2b38403a86454c704f2adcedc5cb4f3` with `open-sse/services/usage/claude.js` and `open-sse/utils/claudeProtocol.js`. The latter already reads 7d_oi status/reset for refusal classification. The usage handler reads endpoint seven_day_* and limits[] windows; upstream adds retained response-header observations with per-window freshness. Verify the end-to-end observation path before calling it a gap or changing shared cooldown semantics.
4. `parity-new-head-review`: review the unrecorded PR batches below, starting with auth/key policy, native image guardrails, unknown-model rejection and streaming error/usage semantics. Release PR #20391 is a moving aggregate: review its constituent commits, not its entire release diff as an independent implementation unit. Compare each new head with its older report and the active local PR stack before assigning work.

961 exclusion occurrences across 94 reports are indexed below. Repetitions are retained as evidence, not separate implementation tasks. The search includes explicit out-of-scope rows and new-feature/not-a-fix rationales with upstream PR links. A cross-reference to an exclusion is not itself a new exclusion. These are review targets; none is labelled already present, not applicable or a verified gap by this index.

Full parity supersedes the old providers-and-connections boundary. Reconsider dashboard, translations, API/key policy, observability, cache/translator behavior, CLI/container and other product features excluded only by that boundary. Architecture-specific and deliberate product-policy differences still need a reasoned decision. Do not turn an absent upstream filename into a not-applicable verdict. New API-key Keenable vs the existing keyless tier (#5887) is one policy review, not a duplicate of the already adopted #5604 public endpoints.

The evidence column links the original exclusion; any other implementation evidence is a reconciliation lead only, and can predate the exclusion.
